brief_data.deck: Druva, the cloud-native data-resilience platform built on AWS and a Leader in Gartner's 2026 Magic Quadrant for Backup and Data Protection for a second year, appointed Anthony Anzevino Chief Commercial and Partner Officer on 28 July 2026 to run global sales, commercial strategy and routes to market.

risks.label: PRIVATE, NO NEW MONEY
risks.detail: The last priced round was April 2021 and the last ARR milestone August 2023; the budget rests on the run-rate, not a raise.
risks.counter: The trigger is the buyer, not the balance sheet: size the entry to the ARR base and part-pay in services.

risks.label: RUBRIK PRECEDENT CUTS BOTH WAYS
risks.detail: A direct rival on a bigger team can make a second data-resilience brand look like a follower.
risks.counter: The debut-team, real-workstream story is a different pitch from a logo on a front-runner.

gridfit.label: PRIME LANE
gridfit.detail: greenfield entry — partner roster being built from zero

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Anthony Anzevino, with Ranga Rajagopalan copied, before the United States GP: confirm the 2027 partner plan, size an Official Data Resilience Partner entry against Cadillac's roster, and agree whether Austin or Las Vegas is the announcement stage.

value.text: Backup and recovery for Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Salesforce and cloud workloads across the team and its new data hub; immutable, air-gapped copies; ransomware-recovery drills run with the team's IT before the season. The team gets resilience it would otherwise have to buy; Druva gets a reference customer that races on television.
value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)

value.text: Druva sells to CIOs, CISOs and managed-service providers; that audience fills a hospitality suite at Austin and Las Vegas and brings channel partners the team's other technology sponsors want to meet.
value.label: Commercial lift for the team

value.text: Co-produced engineering content on protecting a race team's data, a joint story with Core Scientific's data hub, and a customer case study for Druva's enterprise sales.
value.label: Content and ecosystem

value.text: Official Data Resilience Partner designation, sidepod or halo placement, naming of the team's recovery environment, hospitality at the US rounds, and driver and engineering access for Druva's channels.
value.label: What the team gives back

why_now.text: On 28 July 2026 Druva appointed Anthony Anzevino Chief Commercial and Partner Officer, responsible for global sales, commercial strategy and routes to market. He joins from Kaseya, where he was Chief Revenue Officer, after more than 20 years at Commvault, Veeam, AWS, VMware and Dell EMC. The release frames the hire around demand for Druva AI Resilience and the company's second consecutive year as a Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader.
why_now.label: Trigger

why_now.text: A new commercial chief sets the partner and go-to-market plan in his first quarter; a proposal that arrives inside that window is judged as part of the plan rather than against it. The CMO, Ranga Rajagopalan, owns brand spend, so the conversation is a two-seat one from the start.
why_now.label: The first hundred days

why_now.text: Druva has raised $475M, most recently $147M in a Series H led by CDPQ in April 2021 at a valuation above $2B, and passed $200M of SaaS annual recurring revenue in August 2023 with more than 5,000 customers. No newer round or ARR milestone has been published, which is why capacity scores 15 rather than higher.
why_now.label: The business behind it

why_now.text: The United States GP in Austin in late October and the Las Vegas GP in November are the two American rounds left in 2026; teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A deal agreed before Austin can be announced in the US and activated in full for 2027.
why_now.label: Calendar window

why_team.text: Cadillac's inaugural partners are IFS (enterprise software), TWG AI (primary and exclusive AI partner), Core Scientific (Official Data Center Partner, building the team's primary US data hub in Indianapolis), 3M, Tenneco, América Móvil and Tommy Hilfiger. No partner covers backup, recovery or cyber-resilience, and the team table lists that category as open.
why_team.label: An open lane on a greenfield roster

why_team.text: A debut team is building its data estate from scratch: engineering data, simulation output, the collaboration and business systems of a new company, and a new data hub. That estate needs immutable backup and rehearsed recovery before the first race weekend, which is what Druva sells.
why_team.label: Something real to protect

why_team.text: A Santa Clara company on the American team, with enterprise buyers and channel partners to host at Austin and Las Vegas, and a Core Scientific data hub in Indianapolis that Druva's AWS-native platform would sit alongside.
why_team.label: The American story

why_team.text: Rubrik's seat at McLaren shows the category buys F1; Cadillac is the team where a second data-resilience brand is protecting something rather than following a rival.
why_team.label: Precedent without conflict

ruled_out.reason: Rubrik, Druva's direct rival, joined the roster for 2026.
NetApp holds storage and data infrastructure; SentinelOne has departed but the data lane is occupied.
CrowdStrike holds cybersecurity; AWS, TeamViewer and SAP fill the technology roster.
Open but not chosen: VAST's data platform and Keeper's identity security sit next to the lane, and the story is less clean than a greenfield roster.
Open but not chosen: Mphasis's data, cyber and AI services crowd the story.

ruled_out.team: Oracle Red Bull Racing · BWT Alpine
ruled_out.reason: Oracle and Microsoft hold the cloud and data lanes.
HP and IBM cover compute and enterprise technology.
Open but not chosen: no American, data-estate story to match Cadillac's.

brief_data.bottom_line: A >$2B, $200M-ARR data-resilience platform with a new commercial chief in his first hundred days, a rival already on the grid, and a debut American team with an open resilience lane and two US rounds inside the window.

brief_data.the_case_p1: Druva was founded in 2008, is headquartered in Santa Clara with R&D in Pune, and has raised $475M, the last $147M in a Series H led by CDPQ in April 2021 at a valuation above $2B. It passed $200M of SaaS annual recurring revenue in August 2023, with more than 5,000 customers and over six billion backups a year. On 28 July 2026 it hired Anthony Anzevino from Kaseya, where he was Chief Revenue Officer, as Chief Commercial and Partner Officer; his career runs through Commvault, Veeam, AWS, VMware and Dell EMC.
brief_data.the_case_p2: A new commercial owner writes his plan in the first quarter, and Druva's category has already been priced on the grid: Rubrik, its direct rival, joined McLaren for 2026. A sponsorship at Druva is now a two-seat conversation, the commercial chief who arrived in July and a chief marketing officer who came up through Commvault and Dell EMC. The audience is American enterprise IT, and the two United States races close the season.

brief_data.industry_meta: Data Resilience · Cloud Backup & Cyber Recovery SaaS
brief_data.value_content: MODE A - operational. Druva's platform backs up and recovers Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Salesforce and cloud workloads with immutable copies; a new team's estate, from the Indianapolis data hub to the factory's engineering data, needs exactly that, with ransomware-recovery drills before the first race weekend. In return: Official Data Resilience Partner, engineering-content rights, and Austin and Las Vegas hospitality for Druva's enterprise buyers and channel partners.
brief_data.why_team_para: Cadillac's inaugural roster is greenfield: IFS runs enterprise software, TWG AI is the exclusive AI partner, Core Scientific builds the team's primary US data hub in Indianapolis, and no partner covers backup, recovery or cyber-resilience; the lane is open in the team table. A new team building a data estate from scratch, with an American audience at Austin and Las Vegas, is where a US data-resilience company protects something real rather than lending a logo.
brief_data.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Data Resilience Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, spanning the new commercial chief's plan and the team's build-out. Estimated $2-4M a year, part-payable in platform services. Scope: sidepod or halo placement, naming of the team's recovery environment, US-race hospitality, and content on protecting a race team's data.
brief_data.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  Anzevino started on 28 July; the first hundred days of a new commercial chief set the partner and marketing plan for 2027. The United States GP in Austin (late October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the two American rounds left in 2026, and teams close 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter.
brief_data.decision_maker_bio: Anzevino joined on 28 July 2026 from Kaseya, where he was Chief Revenue Officer, to run global sales, commercial strategy and routes to market. Path: Ranga Rajagopalan, Chief Marketing Officer, who owns brand spend; Jaspreet Singh, Founder and CEO; Stephen Manley, Chief Technology Officer, as the technical counterpart.
brief_data.decision_maker_role: Chief Commercial and Partner Officer, Druva
brief_data.opening_angle_quote: “Anthony, Rubrik took a seat at McLaren this year; Cadillac is building its data estate from scratch and has no resilience partner. 25 minutes before Austin to see whether that lane is Druva's?”
